title: Manic patient
stem: Cubicle 10. Ms Fung, 31, was brought by her husband: she has not slept for 4 nights, spent HK$200,000 on luxury goods, and says she is about to become Chief Executive. Assess her and outline management.
notes:
Checked against NICE CG185 (Bipolar disorder, 2014, updated 2023) and the ED approach to mania.

Mania: elevated or irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, flight of ideas, grandiosity (may be delusional), distractibility, disinhibition, risky behaviour (spending, sex, driving), for at least a week (or any duration if hospitalised). Exclude organic causes: thyrotoxicosis, steroids, stimulants, antidepressants, head injury, delirium, and pregnancy (affects drug choice).

ED management: safety, a calm low-stimulus environment, de-escalation; if needed, rapid tranquillisation (oral first: e.g. lorazepam or an antipsychotic; IM options per NICE NG10). Refer to psychiatry; admission (voluntary or under the MHO) for risk. Acute treatment: an antipsychotic (haloperidol, olanzapine, quetiapine or risperidone); stop antidepressants. Lithium and valproate need specialist decisions; valproate must be avoided in women of childbearing potential unless the Pregnancy Prevention Programme is met.

Your notes list 'manic patient' as a topic and have MSE features of mania (pressured speech, flight of ideas, bizarre clothing); nothing conflicts.

steps.label: Talk to her husband
steps.hint: Timeline, sleep, spending, risk, past episodes, drugs, medical.

Change.t: What has changed, and since when?
Change.r: Ten days ago she became very energetic, talking non-stop, barely sleeping for 4 nights.
Spent our savings. Drove at 150 km/h. Quit her job by email.

Background.t: Has she had depression or anything similar before?
Background.r: She was very low after our daughter was born two years ago.

Background.t: Medicines, steroids, drugs, alcohol? Could she be pregnant?
Background.r: Her GP started an antidepressant a month ago. No drugs. We're not trying for a baby.

Observe.r: Bright make-up, many rings, restless, standing up, laughing loudly.

Ask.r: Fantastic! Better than ever! I'm going to run Hong Kong!
Jumps from shoes to politics to the stars with rhyming links.

Ask.t: Any thoughts of harm to yourself or others?
Ask.r: Why would I? I'm unstoppable. Anyone who blocks me will regret it.

Ask.t: Do you think anything is wrong?

steps.label: Plan
steps.hint: Organic screen, calm environment, stop the antidepressant, antipsychotic, psychiatry, admission.

opts.t: Screen for organic causes: TFT, glucose, urine drug screen, pregnancy test, bloods
opts.mark: Organic screen including TFT, drugs and pregnancy test

opts.t: Urgent psychiatry; admission (voluntary, or MHO if she refuses and risk is high)
Start sodium valproate in the ED
opts.r: Valproate is avoided in women of childbearing potential unless the Pregnancy Prevention Programme applies; leave mood stabilisers to psychiatry.

qs.q: Minimum duration of symptoms for a manic episode?
wrong: 4 days, the same as hypomania, if impaired

qs.a: No psychosis and less functional impairment
wrong: A longer duration, at least 2 weeks of symptoms

qs.q: Why avoid valproate in women of childbearing age?

badge.name: Speed Limit
badge.flavor: No sleep, big plans, fast talk: screen organics, calm room, antipsychotic.

options: Early morning waking with low mood

cards.q: What to do with an antidepressant in mania?

options: Slow, with long pauses before each answer

options: Only a serum valproate level at 2 weeks
